subject: Anatomy
summary: The ileum is the distal part of the small intestine, crucial for bile acid reabsorption and immune surveillance. Clinicians must recognize its role in malabsorption, Crohn’s disease, and surgical resections. Understanding its relations helps avoid iatrogenic injury.

sections.p: The ileum is the final segment of the small intestine, extending from the jejunoileal junction to the ileocecal valve. It is a key site for nutrient absorption and immune function.
It begins at the jejunoileal junction and ends at the ileocecal valve. The mucosa has villi and microvilli, and the submucosa contains lymphoid aggregates.
Adjacent structures include the cecum, appendix, and mesenteric vessels. The ileocecal valve separates it from the colon.
Supplied by the ileocolic artery (branch of the superior mesenteric artery) and drained by the ileocolic vein.

t.b: Assesses blood flow; low flow suggests ischemia

sections.p: Parasympathetic via vagus and pelvic splanchnic nerves; sympathetic via mesenteric plexus.
Absorbs bile acids, vitamin B12, and remaining nutrients. It also hosts immune cells that sample luminal antigens.
Common issues include Crohn’s disease, ischemia, and surgical resections. Complications can lead to malabsorption and strictures.
Remember the ileal brake: fat stimulates PYY release, slowing gastric emptying. In surgery, avoid damaging the ileocecal valve.

whenToSeekHelp: Severe abdominal pain with vomiting, signs of obstruction, or bloody diarrhea
Rapid weight loss with malabsorption symptoms

faq.a: Loss or dysfunction of ileal transporters, often due to Crohn’s disease or resection.

faq.q: How is Crohn’s disease diagnosed in the ileum?
faq.a: Endoscopy with biopsy showing transmural inflammation and granulomas; imaging shows strictures.

faq.q: Why is the ileum important for vitamin B12 absorption?
faq.a: Intrinsic factor–B12 complex is absorbed in the terminal ileum via cubilin receptors.

exam: Explain the pathophysiology of bile acid malabsorption after ileal resection.
Describe the ileal brake mechanism and its clinical significance.
Outline the diagnostic workup for suspected ileal Crohn’s disease.
